sections.heading: Why dish soap, scrub pads, and steam mops backfire
sections.body: Dish soap and all-purpose sprays leave residue, so every mop adds to the film instead of lifting it. Abrasive pads and high-alkaline tile strippers cut into the wear layer and leave it permanently cloudy. Steam mops push heat and moisture into the seams. That can loosen glue-down vinyl or swell the core of a floating plank floor.

sections.heading: Signs your dryer vent is clogged with lint

sections.heading: Why the lint screen and a store brush stop short

Lint plus trapped heat is the fire risk, and that is why dryers are a leading source of home fires. A short brush from the hardware store can pack lint deeper into a bend instead of pulling it out.

sections.heading: How we clear a clogged dryer vent from dryer to hood
sections.body: We start at the transition hose behind the dryer and work the full run to the outside hood, pulling lint out instead of pushing it further in. We open the exterior cap, clear the flap, and check that it swings free. Then we run the dryer and confirm air is actually leaving at the hood. If the plastic or foil hose behind the dryer is crushed, we recommend replacing it, even when the long pipe comes out clear.

sections.heading: When cleaning is not enough, and what to tell us

sections.heading: Signs grit is building up in the knots
sections.body: Fold a corner back so the pile opens up. If you see gray dust at the base of the knots, or grit falls out when you tap the back, the rug is wearing under your feet. Other signs are a dull traffic lane, pile that stays flat, and fringe that looks fuzzy or thin. Sharp grit cuts the wool fibers every time someone walks across.

sections.heading: Vacuum with suction only, never a beater bar
sections.body: A beater bar or a rented steam machine can feel like the thorough fix. Both do harm on a hand-knotted rug. The bar pulls knots and frays fringe, and a soaking machine can make dye bleed and leave the foundation wet. Use the suction head only, move in the direction of the pile, skip the fringe or give it one gentle pass, and rotate the rug so the same path is not the only path.

sections.heading: Pads, sunlight, and spills on a wool rug
sections.body: A pad stops the foundation from grinding on the hard floor and keeps the rug from walking. Sun through the same window will fade a dye that no wash can restore, so move the rug or filter the light. Blot spills with a plain white cloth and cool water, and press instead of rubbing. Do not soak a knotted rug and roll it up wet. Leave it flat with air moving over it.

sections.heading: When the plant wash is due, and what to tell us
sections.body: Home care does not remove the grit packed in the knots. That takes a plant wash on a schedule, and we pick the rug up and bring it back. A wash will not repair moth holes, dry rot in the foundation, or dye that has already faded or run. When you call (949) 992-3299 for oriental rug cleaning or pickup, tell us the size, wool or silk, any pet spots, and the last wash date. water-damage-restoration-in-irvine-ca.title: Water-Damaged Carpet: Dry It, Clean It, or Replace It
water-damage-restoration-in-irvine-ca.description: Water-damaged carpet can be dried and cleaned when the water was clean and the pad is saved in time. If not, it is replaced. Call (949) 992-3299.
water-damage-restoration-in-irvine-ca.heroAlt: Water-damaged carpet lifted so the pad can be dried or removed

sections.heading: The water that soaked your carpet decides the outcome
sections.body: Whether water-damaged carpet is saved, cleaned, or torn out depends on what the water was and how long it sat. Clean water from a supply line, caught the same day, often means we extract it, dry or replace the pad, and clean the carpet. Drain water and floodwater that reached the yarn usually mean the carpet and pad come out. We don't fudge the water category to save a room.

sections.heading: Why fans and a shop vac leave the pad wet
sections.body: A shop vac pulls water from the top of the yarn, and fans dry the surface you can touch. The pad underneath holds far more water, and it dries slowly with carpet sitting on top. Mold can start in wet material within 24 to 48 hours. A musty smell or a dark ring near the walls is a sign the pad stayed wet, even if the carpet feels dry.

sections.heading: Extraction, a pad check, then the cleaning
sections.body: First we pull standing water out of the carpet and pad. Then we lift the carpet to check the pad and the subfloor. A wet pad is usually replaced, because once it sours, cleaning the face yarn won't stop the odor. After structural drying, truck-mounted hot-water extraction removes the soil the water carried, and the cleaned carpet dries in 4 to 8 hours.

sections.heading: When to replace it, and what to tell us when you call
sections.body: If the water came from a drain, a toilet, or outside, or if it sat for days, plan on replacing the carpet and pad. We can't promise cleaning will save them. You can pull the carpet back and run fans if the power is safe, but don't lay it back down on a wet pad. Call (949) 992-3299 and tell us where the water came from, how long it sat, and which rooms it reached. We'll tell you when we can get there. your-home-needs-carpet-protector-treatme.title: Carpet Protector After Hot-Water Extraction Cleaning
your-home-needs-carpet-protector-treatme.description: Carpet protector after hot-water extraction gives fresh spills less time to bond with dry fiber. Apply it once the carpet is dry. Call (949) 992-3299.
your-home-needs-carpet-protector-treatme.heroAlt: Liquid beading on carpet fibers after a protector treatment

sections.heading: What carpet protector does and does not do
sections.body: Carpet protector is a fluorochemical or similar finish sprayed on fiber that is already clean. On a protected carpet, spilled juice beads up for a moment before it wets the yarn, so you have time to blot. It does not make the carpet stain-proof, and it does nothing for soil already down in the backing. If spills soak in the second they land, the old protection is probably gone.

sections.heading: Why a hardware-store spray can falls short
sections.body: Most people spray a can of protector on carpet that has not been rinsed. That coats the soil along with the fiber. Coverage also tends to be heavy in one spot and missing a foot away. Any protector applied before an extraction just gets rinsed out, so the order matters: clean first, then protect.

sections.heading: How protector goes on after the truck-mounted rinse
sections.body: We clean with truck-mounted hot-water extraction using EPA Safer Choice cleaning solutions, then recover as much water as the machine can pull. The carpet should be dry enough that the protector sits on the yarn instead of wicking into a damp backing. We spray it evenly and groom it into the pile, paying extra attention to entries and the lanes where feet land. Dry time runs about 4 to 8 hours, and traffic wears protector off those lanes first, so it is reapplied at the next cleaning rather than treated as permanent.

sections.heading: Which rooms need protector and which can skip it
sections.body: Dining rooms, kids' rooms, and light colors benefit. A dark, low-traffic bedroom often does not, and protector will not hide a set stain or bring back crushed, worn yarn. When you call (949) 992-3299, tell us which rooms are light or spill-prone, what the carpet is made of if you know, and whether it was protected before.
